decriminalization.summary: Sex between people of the same sex was decriminalised in 1969 by the Criminal Law Amendment Act. The same age of consent — 16 — now applies to everyone.

marriage.summary: Marriage for civil purposes is the lawful union of two persons, under the Civil Marriage Act 2005. Religious officials may refuse to perform a marriage that conflicts with their beliefs.

genderRecognition.summary: Gender identity and gender expression are protected grounds under the Canadian Human Rights Act since 2017. Federal documents such as passports allow an X marker, but birth certificates are issued by provinces and territories, so the process varies by where you live.

sources.label: IRCC — changing the sex or gender designation on a passport

conversionTherapy.summary: Conversion practices are a criminal offence under s. 320.1 of the Criminal Code, added in 2022. The offence also covers advertising them, profiting from them, and taking a child out of Canada for them.

asylum.summary: Claims can be based on sexual orientation or gender identity as membership of a particular social group under s. 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. The Immigration and Refugee Board has a guideline on handling these cases.
